title: EDACS (Emergency Department Assessment of Chest Pain Score)
keywords: low risk under 16 points plus no new ischemia plus negative 0/2h troponin
pleuritic and palpation-reproducible pain subtract points
sources: Than M, et al. Development and validation of the Emergency Department Assessment of Chest pain Score and 2 h accelerated diagnostic protocol. Emerg Med Australas. 2014;26(1):34-41.
Than M, et al. Effectiveness of EDACS versus ADAPT accelerated diagnostic pathways for chest pain: a pragmatic randomized controlled trial. Ann Emerg Med. 2016;68(1):93-102.

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (Content audit 2026-09-14, Batch 3). Point values verified via WebSearch against the original 2014 derivation paper before building.

purpose: Risk-stratify ED chest pain for possible early discharge without stress testing, when combined with two negative troponins 2 hours apart and no new ischemia on ECG (the full EDACS-ADP).
notes: EDACS alone gives the score below. The full accelerated diagnostic pathway (EDACS-ADP) requires ALL THREE: EDACS < 16, no new ischemic changes on ECG, and troponin negative at both 0h and 2h. Any one of those failing means the patient is NOT low risk regardless of the EDACS number — this calculator scores EDACS only, it does not track the ECG/troponin arms for you.

items.label: Known coronary artery disease, OR ≥ 3 risk factors (HTN, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, current smoker, family history of premature CAD)
Pain radiates to arm, shoulder, neck, or jaw
Pain occurs with, or is worsened by, inspiration

interpretation.label: Low risk (< 16)
interpretation.detail: Eligible for the EDACS-ADP IF also no new ischemia on ECG AND troponin negative at both 0h and 2h. Meeting all three supports early discharge without provocative testing.

interpretation.label: Not low risk (≥ 16)
interpretation.detail: Does not qualify for the accelerated pathway regardless of ECG/troponin results — manage per standard ACS workup.

buildNote: engine: additive with the age band represented as a 10-option select item, matching the ASPECTS/Bishop/Child-Pugh pattern from prior batches rather than a formula-engine step function — this is how the score is actually presented and used at the bedside (pick your band, don't compute). Companion to heart-score / modified-shock-index; not a replacement for either.
